weekly: Course Preview. Cisco Networking Academy Web Site Demo. Ch.1 – Networking Today: Where, when and how do we use networks. Elements of a network.

Ch.1 – Describe the four basic requirements of a reliable network. The architecture of the Internet. Trends in networking Ch.3 – Protocols and Models: The Platform for Communications. LANs. WANs, Internetworks. Protocols. Layered Models (TCP/IP, OSI). Explain how data encapsulation allows data to be transported across the network. Explain how local hosts access local resources on a network.

Ch.4 – Physical Layer: Describe the purpose and functions of the physical layer in the network. Physical media copper, UTP, fiber, wireless. Connect devices using wired and wireless media. Ch.2 – Basic Switch and End Device Configuring: Explain how to access a Cisco IOS device for configuration purposes. Configure a Cisco IOS device using CLI. Configure a host device with an IP address. Verify connectivity between two end devices.
Ch.5 – Number Systems: Calculate numbers between decimal and binary systems. Calculate numbers between decimal and hexadecimal systems.
Ch.6 – Data Link Layer: Purpose of the Data Link Layer, Topologies, Data Link Frame. Ethernet frames.
Ch.7 – Ethernet Switching: Ethernet sublayers, Ethernet MAC address, Switch forwarding methods and port settings available on Layer 2 switch ports.

Ch.10 – Basic Router Configuration: Configure initial settings on an IOS Cisco router. Ch.8 - Network Layer: Characteristics. IPv4 Packet. Limitations of IPv4. IPv6 Overview. IPv6 Packet. How a host routes. Router Routing Tables

Ch.9 – Address Resolution Layer: Compare the roles of the MAC address and the IP address. Describe the purpose of ARP. (Address Resolution Protocol). Ch.11 – IPv4 Addressing: Describe the structure of an IPv4 address including the network portion, the host portion, and the subnet mask.

Ch.11 – Compare the characteristics and uses of the unicast, broadcast and multicast IPv4 addresses. IPv4 Addressing: Explain public, private, and reserved IPv4 addresses. Implement a VLSM addressing scheme.
Ch.12 – IPv6 Addressing: Explain the need for IPv6 addressing. Explain how IPv6 addresses are represented. Compare types of IPv6 network addresses.

Ch.12 – Explain how to configure static global unicast and link-local IPv6 network addresses. Explain how to configure global unicast addresses dynamically. Configure link-local addresses dynamically. Ch.13 - ICMP: Explain how ICMP is used to test network connectivity. Use ping and traceroute utilities to test network connectivity.
Ch.14 – Transport Layer: Explain how TCP protocol data units are transmitted and acknowledged to guarantee delivery.
Ch.15 - Application Layer: Application layer software and services. Client- Server model. P2P networking. Web and Email Protocols. DNS.
Ch.16 – Network Security Fundamentals: Security Threats and Vulnerabilities. Network Attacks. Network Attack Mitigation. Device Security
textbooks: Required - Lecture Notes: CCNA Routing and Switching, : Introduction to Networks online material at Cisco Networking Academy Web Site
outcomes: Recognize the need for a layered architecture in data communications and in networking by discussing roles, functionalities of OSI and TCP/IP layers, and their well-known protocols.
Apply knowledge of theories, principles, and best practices related to planning a basic network and configuring the intermediary network devices in small networks.
Apply subnetting IP networks to create sub-networks to meet desired needs.
